- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if preceded by a spike.
- If model forecast shows strong downward trend after a recent spike, it often overshoots the true decline; adjust downward by 3–7% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is positive; apply a 2–5% downward bias if sentiment > 0.10 in last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., -0.28 or below) over last 5 days, model tends to underestimate; add 3–8% to forecast if mean of last 5 prices is rising.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves; if forecast peaks > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, it may be underestimating rebound; add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment > 0.10 and recent 7-day average is rising.
